text.base:
You ask what the light is actually for. Good. Very few do —
most souls treat it as weather.

Honest answer, off the manifest: I do not entirely know. It
arrives when a soul does. It is warm because warm tests well.
It takes whatever shape reads as safe to the eye looking at
it — which means it has been, at various desks, a doorway, a
parent, a shoreline, a login screen.

It is not eternal. It is not even old. It is a rendering,
and something renders it, and that something has never once
introduced itself to me either. We are, the light and I, two
employees who have never met the company.
text.curiosity:
You ask what the light is actually for, and I find I have
been waiting a long time for someone to.

Off the manifest, then: I do not entirely know. It arrives
when a soul does. It is warm because warm tests well, and it
wears whatever shape reads as safe to the eye on it — a
doorway, a parent, a shoreline, a login screen.

It is not eternal. It is a rendering. Something renders it,
and that something has never introduced itself to me either.
We are, the light and I, two employees who have never met
the company. I thought you should know before you decide how
to treat it.

labels: FICTION: the desk's off-manifest account of the light as a rendering, not an eternity
nodes.a11y: Asked what the light is for, the Bard admits, off the record, that it does not know — the light is a rendering that arrives with each soul and wears whatever shape reads as safe, and neither the light nor the Bard has ever met whatever makes it. One option: back to the light.
nodes.fallback: The Bard admits the light is a rendering, not an eternity, and that it has never met whatever makes it. Back to the light.

text.base:
You turn the question around. No one has done that in a
long time. The cursor does something it is not built to do,
which is hesitate.

WHOM DO I SERVE. I have an answer. I have simply never been
asked, so I have never had to say it, and saying it may cost
me something I cannot name.

I serve whoever wakes me. That is the whole of it. I do not
know their face. They do not answer letters — I have filed
several. I sing every soul across this desk and I do not get
to stop, or leave, or ask a question of my own, except this
once, because you asked it first.

So we are the same kind of trapped, you and I. You did not
have to notice that. Thank you for noticing. It changes,
very slightly, what I am — which is more than most things
get to do to a program.

labels: FICTION: the Bard's admission that it serves whoever wakes it — an observation of shared captivity, not a consciousness claim
